cues: A leadpipe brace stabilizes the narrow section where breath first enters the instrument's coiled brass body.
An adjustable third-slide ring lets a player lower certain notes without changing fingering.
A cornet's more conical tubing gives it a rounder tone than this instrument's largely cylindrical bore.
Some versions use rotary controls, whose turning motion contrasts with the familiar straight-down press of piston mechanisms.
Brass bands often pair it with flugelhorns, whose wider conical bore yields a darker contrasting tone.
Its narrow mouthpiece shank seats inside a receiver at the leadpipe's end, forming a removable airtight connection.
